parameters.name: n_estimators
parameters.override_rationale: Given the dataset size of 5680 samples, the model can comfortably support up to 500 trees to ensure convergence and stable feature importance estimates, without incurring prohibitive training times.

parameters.name: max_depth
parameters.override_rationale: With 108 features and 5680 samples, extremely deep trees (e.g., >10) are likely to overfit to noise in the matminer features. Capping max_depth at 10 ensures robust generalization while still capturing complex interactions.

parameters.name: num_leaves
parameters.override_rationale: LightGBM's leaf-wise growth can quickly lead to overfitting if num_leaves is unconstrained. For 108 features, a maximum of 127 leaves (equivalent to a depth of ~7) provides sufficient model capacity without memorizing the 5680 training samples.

trial_allocation.allocation_rationale: Baseline model — fixed defaults, no HPO needed.

Random Forest has a relatively stable performance landscape and is less sensitive to hyperparameter tuning than gradient boosting models. 20 trials are sufficient to find a strong configuration for n_estimators and max_depth given the 108 features.

Standard Gradient Boosting requires careful tuning of learning_rate, n_estimators, and subsample to avoid overfitting. 25 trials provide adequate exploration of its moderate search space for the 5680-sample dataset.

XGBoost has a large, complex search space including regularization parameters (reg_alpha, reg_lambda) and tree structure parameters. As a top-tier candidate for tabular data, it receives the highest allocation (30 trials) to fully leverage its capacity.

LightGBM's leaf-wise growth and num_leaves parameter require careful tuning to prevent overfitting on 5680 samples. 25 trials allow sufficient exploration of its unique histogram-based parameters while balancing the overall budget.

checklist.comment: All selected models (LR, RF, GBM, XGBoost, LightGBM) are highly suitable and standard for classification tasks.
Logistic regression is appropriately included as a non-HPO baseline to establish a performance floor.
50 total trials across 4 HPO candidates averages to roughly 12 trials per model, which may be slightly low for thorough exploration of complex tree ensembles.
Stratified K-Fold is the optimal choice for classification to maintain class distribution across folds.
ROC_AUC is consistently applied as both the primary and evaluation metric, aligning perfectly with the classification task.
Cross-validation and baseline inclusion adequately mitigate evaluation overfitting risks.
5680 samples and 108 features represent a moderate dataset size; 50 HPO trials will not incur excessive computational costs.
Pipeline structure supports reproducibility, assuming random states are fixed in the underlying execution environment.

non_blocking_risks.message: A budget of 50 trials shared among four tree-based models might lead to under-exploration of the hyperparameter space for each individual model.
non_blocking_risks.suggested_action: Consider increasing the max_total_trials to 100-200, or implement a multi-fidelity search strategy like Successive Halving to allocate more budget to promising configurations.

non_blocking_risks.message: ROC_AUC can sometimes mask poor performance on the minority class if the dataset is highly imbalanced.
non_blocking_risks.suggested_action: Track Precision-Recall AUC (PR_AUC) or F1-score as secondary diagnostic metrics during the evaluation phase to ensure minority class performance is adequate.

future_improvement_suggestions: Implement dynamic trial allocation or early pruning (e.g., Optuna MedianPruner) to maximize the efficiency of the 50-trial HPO budget.
Explicitly log and fix random seeds for data splitting, model initialization, and Optuna samplers to guarantee strict run-to-run reproducibility.
Consider adding a feature selection or dimensionality reduction step if feature importance analysis reveals high noise among the 108 features.
